title: Check yourself: What changes in jPOS 3

questions.stem: A QMUX on jPOS 2.1.7 has <key>41, 11</key> and, copied from the current jPOS documentation, <key mti="01" pcode="300000">41, 37</key>. A gateway sends 0100 pre-authorizations with field 3 = 000000, fields 11 and 41, and no field 37. Which fields make up their key?

options.text: Fields 41 and 11, since the message's field 3 doesn't match the override
options.says: 2.1.7 reads only the mti attribute; pcode is ignored, so the override applies to every 01xx (13.2).

options.text: Fields 41, 11 and 37, since an override adds its fields to the default key
options.says: An override replaces the key for its MTI class; it doesn't add to the default (13.2).

options.text: Field 41 alone, since the override applies and a field the message lacks is left out
options.says: The pcode is ignored, the override's 41, 37 applies, and the absent 37 is skipped, so pre-authorizations from one terminal collide (13.2).

options.text: Fields 41 and 37, since the override applies and a field the message lacks is padded with zeros
options.says: A missing key field is skipped, not padded; and pcode is ignored, so the override applies to every 01xx (13.2).

origin.section: 13.2 A jPOS 3 Descriptor Deploys on 2.1.7, and What 2.1.7 Doesn't Read Does Nothing

questions.stem: A descriptor declares, in this order: OpenJournal (starts a database transaction and puts TX in the Context), RecordSale, Authorize, CloseJournal (commits and removes TX), SendResponse (holds the answer while TX is set). It is moved unchanged to a TransactionManager that calls commit in reverse declaration order. Authorize approves a sale. What does the terminal receive?

options.text: The approval, since every participant prepared and the order of commit calls doesn't change what is sent
options.says: The order decides whether SendResponse finds TX set; reversed, it runs before CloseJournal and sends nothing (13.3).

options.text: The approval, since SendResponse waits until CloseJournal has finished before it sends
options.says: SendResponse doesn't wait: with TX set it sends nothing and returns (13.3, unit s9).

options.text: Nothing, since SendResponse runs its commit before CloseJournal runs its own
options.says: Reversed, SendResponse commits before CloseJournal, finds TX and sends nothing; the sale is then committed and the terminal reverses it (13.3).

options.text: Nothing, since a reverse-order commit turns the approved sale into an abort
options.says: The order of commit calls doesn't turn a commit into an abort; the sale is committed, unanswered (13.3).

origin.section: 13.3 The Same Descriptor Can Behave Differently on the Two Lines

questions.stem: On jPOS 2.1.7, a participant calls mux.request(m, 5000) on a QMUX whose channel has lost its connection, so isConnected() is false. What does the call do?

options.text: It throws an ISOException at once, so the participant can answer without waiting
options.says: That is what the jPOS 3 documentation describes; in 2.1.7 send throws, request doesn't (13.3).

options.text: It throws an ISOException after 5 seconds, since the message expires unsent
options.says: An unanswered request returns null when its timeout ends; it doesn't throw (13.3).

options.text: It returns null after 5 seconds, since the message waits in the queue until its timeout
options.says: QMUX 2.1.7 queues the request and returns null after the timeout (13.3).

options.text: It returns null at once, since nothing can be written to a channel that is down
options.says: request doesn't check the link; it waits the whole timeout (13.3).

origin.section: 13.3 The Same Descriptor Can Behave Differently on the Two Lines

questions.stem: On jPOS 2.1.7, a helper reads TransactionManager.getContext(). A participant pauses after an asynchronous mux.request and calls the helper from its ISOResponseListener when the issuer's answer arrives. What does the helper get there?

options.text: The paused transaction's Context, since the listener was registered by that transaction
options.says: The accessor reads a thread-local, which the listener's thread doesn't have (13.4).

options.text: The Context of the session's last transaction, since a thread-local keeps its last value
options.says: The callback doesn't run on a session's thread, and the TransactionManager clears the value after each call (13.4).

options.text: null, since the callback runs on a thread on which nothing was stored for it
options.says: The value is set only around the TransactionManager's own calls; the answer arrives on another thread (13.4).

options.text: null, since a paused transaction's Context is withheld until the transaction resumes
options.says: Nothing is withheld; the Context is reachable through handBack. The accessor fails because of the thread (13.4).

origin.section: 13.4 Code That Finds Its Transaction Through a Thread-Local Breaks on Both Lines
